# @codenhub/icons/play

## Functions

### bindIconPlayback

```ts
export declare function bindIconPlayback(root?: Document | Element | undefined, options?: IconPlaybackOptions): () => void;
```

Plays every `ic-on-hover` icon in a subtree from the start each time its trigger is hovered or gets visible keyboard focus.

The trigger is the icon itself, its parent, or any ancestor carrying `ic-trigger`, the same rule the `ic-on-hover` CSS follows. CSS alone already restarts glyph motion and looping artwork; this is what replays one-shot artwork, such as a Line MD draw-in, on every hover rather than once per page. Icons inserted later are covered. Importing the module touches no globals; calling it outside a browser without a root returns a no-op.

**Parameters**

- `root` — Subtree holding the triggers and their icons. Defaults to `document` in a browser.
- `options` — Class and custom property prefix.

**Returns** — A function that removes the listeners and the inline overrides they left.

### playIcon

```ts
export declare function playIcon(element: Element, options?: IconPlaybackOptions): void;
```

Plays one icon's motion from the start: its `ic-anim-*` glyph motion and its animated artwork, whichever it has.

Does nothing when the device requests reduced motion. Glyph motion restarts, whether running or finished, by clearing the element's `animation-name` for one style recalculation; this forces style. Artwork in a CSS mask restarts from a fresh data URL set inline as `--ic-mask`, because a browser does not restart an image it has already shown; [`bindIconPlayback`](#bindiconplayback) removes that override when the trigger ends. An inline `<svg>` restarts with `setCurrentTime(0)`. Verified in Chrome; Firefox and Safari are untested.

**Parameters**

- `element` — Icon to play. Elements with neither are ignored.
- `options` — Class and custom property prefix.
